title: H. A Certain Scientific Tree Problem

legend: Misaka has come up with a very good problem for this contest. Unfortunately, that problem already exists (on at least 3 different online judges!) so she has to add a creative twist to it!

Consider a full binary tree of depth d%%ZSMJ0%%. Remember a full binary tree with depth d%%ZSMJ1%% has 2d−1%%ZSMJ2%% nodes and there is an edge from each node u%%ZSMJ3%% (2≤u≤2d−1)%%ZSMJ4%% to its parent ⌊u2⌋%%ZSMJ5%%. Misaka asks you to find the sum of distances between every pair of nodes on the tree.
Formally if n=2d−1%%ZSMJ6%% (n=#%%ZSMJ7%% nodes on the tree), compute:
where dist(i,j)%%ZSMJ9%% is the minimum number of edges on any path between node i%%ZSMJ10%% to node j%%ZSMJ11%%.
input: The first line will contain one integer T%%ZSMJ12%% denoting the number of multitests (1≤T≤5)%%ZSMJ13%%.
The first line of each test will contain one integer d%%ZSMJ14%% the depth of the binary tree (1≤d≤105)%%ZSMJ15%%.
Testcases in subtasks are numbered 1−20%%ZSMJ16%% with samples skipped.

Testcases 1−4%%ZSMJ17%% satisfy i%%ZSMJ18%%'th multitest of the j%%ZSMJ19%%'th testcase has d=(j−1)⋅5+i%%ZSMJ20%%. For instance testcase 2%%ZSMJ21%% will consist of d=[6,7,8,9,10]%%ZSMJ22%% across the 5%%ZSMJ23%% multitests.
The remaining testcases do not satisfy any additional constraints.
output: Output one integer S%%ZSMJ28%% per testcase denoting the sum of distances across all pairs of nodes on the tree. Since this number may be very large, please find it modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ29%%.
note: In the first sample, the tree only has 1%%ZSMJ30%% node. As dist(1,1)=0%%ZSMJ31%%, the answer would just be 0%%ZSMJ32%%.
In the second sample, there are 3%%ZSMJ33%% nodes on a full binary tree with depth 2%%ZSMJ34%%. There are edges 1−2%%ZSMJ35%% and 1−3%%ZSMJ36%%.
